title: Pullback of a pointed etale chart diagram through arbitrary base change and open restrictions
statement:
Let $f_0:X_0\to S_0$ and $Y\to T$ be morphisms of schemes [def-pc-scheme]. Suppose schemes $U_0,V_0$ carry etale morphisms $p_0:U_0\to X_0$, $e_0:V_0\to S_0$ [def-weil-etale-morphism], morphisms $w_0:U_0\to V_0$, $\tau_0:V_0\to T$, and an etale $V_0$-morphism $m_0:U_0\to Y\times_{T,\tau_0}V_0$ [def-pc-fibre-product], such that $e_0\circ w_0=f_0\circ p_0$ and $\operatorname{pr}_{V_0}\circ m_0=w_0$. Fix $u_0\in U_0$ and put $x_0=p_0(u_0)$. Let $f:X\to S$ be any scheme morphism, let $X^\circ\subseteq X$ and $S^\circ\subseteq S$ be open subschemes [def-weil-open-immersion] with $f(X^\circ)\subseteq S^\circ$, and let $c:S^\circ\to S_0$ be a morphism together with an $S^\circ$-isomorphism $X^\circ\cong X_0\times_{S_0}S^\circ$. Fix $x\in X^\circ$ whose projection to $X_0$ is $x_0$. Define
$$V=V_0\times_{S_0}S^\circ,\qquad U=U_0\times_{X_0}X^\circ.$$
Then the projections followed by the open inclusions give etale morphisms $e:V\to S$ and $p:U\to X$. There are canonical isomorphisms
$$U\cong U_0\times_{S_0}S^\circ\cong U_0\times_{V_0}V,$$
a morphism $w:U\to V$ and an etale $V$-morphism $m:U\to Y\times_{T,\tau}V$, where $\tau=\tau_0\circ\operatorname{pr}_{V_0}$, satisfying $e\circ w=f\circ p$ and $\operatorname{pr}_V\circ m=w$. The map $m$ is the base change of $m_0$ under these canonical isomorphisms. There exists $u\in U$ projecting to the specified $u_0$ and $x$, so in particular $p(u)=x$. For every $a\in\Gamma(T,\mathcal O_T)$, writing $h_0=\tau_0^*a$ and $h=\operatorname{pr}_{V_0}^*h_0$, one has $h=\tau^*a$.

proof.text: Write $f^\circ:X^\circ\to S^\circ$ for the restriction of $f$, $\alpha:X^\circ\xrightarrow{\sim}X_0\times_{S_0}S^\circ$ for the given isomorphism, and $q:X^\circ\to X_0$ for its first projection. Let $a:U\to U_0$ and $t:U\to X^\circ$ be the defining projections, and put $b=f^\circ t$. Set $P=U_0\times_{S_0}S^\circ$, using $f_0p_0=e_0w_0$ as the structure map of $U_0$. The map $U\to P$ is $(a,b)$. Its inverse sends the projections $(a',b')$ of $P$ to the pair $(a',\alpha^{-1}(p_0a',b'))$ defining a map to $U$. Both composites are identities because they preserve the two defining projections. Likewise $P\to U_0\times_{V_0}V$ is $(a',(w_0a',b'))$, and its inverse takes $(a',v)$ to $(a',\operatorname{pr}_{S^\circ}v)$. These are inverse by the same projection check. Every parenthesized pair here is a pair of scheme morphisms; existence and equality follow from the universal property in [def-pc-fibre-product]. These give precisely the asserted canonical isomorphisms.

source.place: Tag 0CBY, lemma-etale-local-structure-nodal-family, first proof, first paragraph; expansion of the base-change identification using Schemes Tag 01JP, definition-fibre-product

proof.text: The projection $V\to S^\circ$ is the base change of $e_0$, and $t:U\to X^\circ$ is the base change of $p_0$. Both are etale by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-scheme-base-change], whose arbitrary-base-change hypothesis permits the given $c$ and $q$. The inclusions $i_S:S^\circ\hookrightarrow S$ and $i_X:X^\circ\hookrightarrow X$ are open immersions, hence etale, and etale morphisms compose by clauses (1)--(2) of [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation]. Thus $e=i_S\operatorname{pr}_{S^\circ}$ and $p=i_Xt$ are etale.

Put $Z_0=Y\times_TV_0$, $Z=Y\times_TV$, and $y_0=\operatorname{pr}_Ym_0$. Step 1 defines $w=(w_0a,b):U\to V$. Define $m=(y_0a,w):U\to Z$ and $r=(\operatorname{pr}_Y,\operatorname{pr}_{V_0}\operatorname{pr}_V):Z\to Z_0$. These pairs are compatible over $T$ since $m_0$ is over $V_0$ and $\tau=\tau_0\operatorname{pr}_{V_0}$. They satisfy $rm=m_0a$ and $\operatorname{pr}_Vm=w$. To check the square $(m,a,r,m_0)$ is cartesian, take any scheme $Q$ with maps $A:Q\to U_0$, $B:Q\to Z$ satisfying $m_0A=rB$. Their $V_0$ projections give $w_0A=\operatorname{pr}_{V_0}\operatorname{pr}_VB$, so Step 1 and [def-pc-fibre-product] give a unique $L:Q\to U$ with $aL=A$ and $wL=\operatorname{pr}_VB$. The $Y$ projections of the same equality give $y_0A=\operatorname{pr}_YB$; hence $mL=B$ by the universal property of $Z$. Uniqueness follows from the projections of $U_0\times_{V_0}V$. This proves that this specified $m$ is the base change of $m_0$, including its compatibility with the model diagram.

source.place: Tag 0CBY, lemma-etale-local-structure-nodal-family, first proof, first paragraph; expansion of the base change of the etale model map using Schemes Tag 01JP, definition-fibre-product

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-etale-scheme-base-change] to the etale scheme morphism $m_0:U_0\to Z_0$ and the arbitrary scheme morphism $r:Z\to Z_0$. The cartesian square established in Step 3 therefore makes $m$ etale. It is a $V$-morphism because $\operatorname{pr}_Vm=w$. Also $ew=i_Sb=i_Sf^\circ t=fi_Xt=fp$, by the restriction identity $i_Sf^\circ=fi_X$. This proves all asserted diagram identities.

source.place: Tag 02GO, lemma-base-change-etale; applied to the cartesian square of Step 3

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-base-change-image] to $p_0:U_0\to X_0$, $q:X^\circ\to X_0$, their fibre product $U$ with projections $a,t$, and the singleton subset $C=\{u_0\}$. It gives $t(a^{-1}(\{u_0\}))=q^{-1}(p_0(\{u_0\}))$. Since $q(x)=x_0=p_0(u_0)$, $x$ belongs to the right side. Membership in the left side supplies $u\in U$ with $a(u)=u_0$ and $t(u)=x$. Thus $p(u)=x$ in $X$. No equality of residue fields or rational-point lifting is required.

source.place: Tag 01S1, lemma-base-change-surjective, proof, subset-image identity; Tag 0495, lemma-when-point-maps-to-pair

proof.text: For a scheme morphism, pullback of global regular functions is the map on structure-sheaf sections; composition of scheme morphisms [def-pc-scheme] composes these maps contravariantly. Thus, for every $a\in\Gamma(T,\mathcal O_T)$, $\operatorname{pr}_{V_0}^*(\tau_0^*a)=(\tau_0\operatorname{pr}_{V_0})^*a=\tau^*a$. This is the required equality $h=\tau^*a$.
